categories.main_business_segments: Westlake Corporation operates in two principal segments: Performance and Essential Materials, which includes vinyls, chlor-alkali, polyethylene, epoxy, and related chemicals; and Housing and Infrastructure Products, which includes building products such as siding, trim, roofing, windows, PVC pipes and fittings, and PVC compounds. These segments are highly integrated, with significant downstream integration from basic chemicals into finished products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes large-scale petrochemical and polymer production technologies, including ethylene crackers (primarily using ethane feedstock), chlor-alkali electrolysis, vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) synthesis, and autoclave technology for specialty polyethylene. Westlake also employs proprietary and licensed processes for epoxy resins and advanced compounding, with a focus on efficiency, recycling, and sustainability (e.g., GreenVin bio-attributed PVC).
categories.primary_customers_markets: Westlake serves a diverse customer base including large chemical processors, plastics fabricators, building product distributors, contractors, municipalities, and OEMs. Key end markets are residential and commercial construction, packaging (flexible and rigid), automotive, healthcare, water treatment, wind energy, coatings, and various consumer and industrial goods sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with major manufacturing facilities in North America (primarily the US and Canada), Europe (notably Germany and the Netherlands), and Asia (including China, Taiwan, and South Korea). Sales are concentrated in the US but also significant in Canada, Germany, China, Italy, and other international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Westlake is a vertically integrated manufacturer, operating both upstream (basic chemicals like ethylene, chlorine, caustic soda) and downstream (PVC, polyethylene, epoxy, and finished building products). The company controls much of its raw material supply and converts these into higher value-added products, occupying positions from raw materials through to end-use products.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding downstream integration, pursuing acquisitions (e.g., Hexion Epoxy, Boral, LASCO, Dimex), and developing innovative and sustainable products such as recycled-content materials and lower-carbon PVC. R&D focuses on product and process innovation, sustainability (including emissions reduction targets), and supporting customer needs for advanced materials in high-growth applications like wind energy and lightweight automotive components.
categories.revenue_model: Westlake generates revenue primarily through the sale of commodity and specialty chemicals, polymers, and finished building products. Revenue streams include direct product sales to industrial customers, distributors, and fabricators, as well as internal transfers between segments. The company also licenses technology and receives fixed-margin ethylene sales through its partnership structure.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include global chemical and materials companies such as Dow, ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell, Formosa Plastics, Olin, INOVYN, Huntsman, and others. Westlake is the second-largest producer of both chlor-alkali and PVC globally, positioning it as a leading integrated chlorovinyls producer with strong market share in North America and Europe, and a growing presence in specialty epoxies and building products.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Westlake reported net sales of $15.8 billion and net income attributable to the company of $2.25 billion, with EBITDA of $4.18 billion. The company has demonstrated strong growth through acquisitions and organic expansion, with a significant increase in both revenue and profitability over the past three years. As of year-end 2022, total assets were $20.6 billion and the company employed approximately 15,920 people.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Westlake emphasizes its vertical integration, cost leadership, and ability to deliver a broad portfolio of essential and performance materials with consistent quality and reliability. The company differentiates through downstream integration, sustainability initiatives (e.g., recycled and bio-attributed products), and innovation in specialty applications such as wind energy, automotive, and advanced building materials, providing customers with value-added, sustainable solutions.
